No png and no anchor for that facing, so the renderer hides the piece on it (the beard precedent, v2.3.1530). jog fitted by tools/tune_headwear.py --fit-pose jog: the jog sheets draw the head at a different size from the idle sheets, so scaleByPose carries headWidth(jog)/headWidth(stand) with the renderer's blanket poseTraitMul divided back out, and poseNudge scales the placement about the crown so the band does not slide down the face. mine fitted by tools/tune_headwear.py --fit-pose mine: the mine sheets draw the head at a different size from the idle sheets, so scaleByPose carries headWidth(mine)/headWidth(stand) with the renderer's blanket poseTraitMul divided back out, and poseNudge scales the placement about the crown so the band does not slide down the face. fish fitted by tools/tune_headwear.py --fit-pose fish: the fish sheets draw the head at a different size from the idle sheets, so scaleByPose carries headWidth(fish)/headWidth(stand) with the renderer's blanket poseTraitMul divided back out, and poseNudge scales the placement about the crown so the band does not slide down the face. hit fitted by tools/tune_headwear.py --fit-pose hit: the hit sheets draw the head at a different size from the idle sheets, so scaleByPose carries headWidth(hit)/headWidth(stand) with the renderer's blanket poseTraitMul divided back out, and poseNudge scales the placement about the crown so the band does not slide down the face. pickup fitted by tools/tune_headwear.py --fit-pose pickup: the pickup sheets draw the head at a different size from the idle sheets, so scaleByPose carries headWidth(pickup)/headWidth(stand) with the renderer's blanket poseTraitMul divided back out, and poseNudge scales the placement about the crown so the band does not slide down the face. v2.3.2395: crownNudge.southwest x -14 -> -22 (owner: "In southwest view the eyeglass needs to hang off the eye more it's too far in the middle of the face").  At -14 the lens sat almost entirely inside the face, immediately beside the near eye, which is exactly the 'middle of the face' reading.  The SOUTH facing is the one the owner is happy with and it hangs roughly HALF the lens past the head's left silhouette; -22 reproduces that proportion in the 3/4 view. Chosen from a rendered sweep of -14/-18/-22/-26 against the south cell as the reference, not from arithmetic: two attempts to compute the overhang analytically both went wrong, once by re-implementing _placeTrait by hand (the very thing preview_headwear.py's header warns is a second opinion rather than a check) and once by measuring the skull's widest point instead of the face at the eye row.  -26 was too far: the lens leaves the eye and the piece reads as floating beside the head rather than clamped on it.  v2.3.2411: crownNudge.south x -12 -> -8 (owner: "The south facing monocle needs to be nudged a bit to the right too").  Chosen from a RENDERED sweep of ten values (-16 -12 -10 -8 -6 -4 -2 0 +4 +12) against the south cell, driven to south through the creator preview -- which opens on SOUTHWEST, so the facing was proved each run from the bare body's own head-band symmetry (asym 0.022 at 390x844, 0.029 at 390x664, both under the 0.06 face-on threshold) rather than assumed.  Sign convention was RENDERED, not read: x -12 puts the lens left edge at canvas 308 and x +12 at 386, so increasing x moves the lens RIGHT.  The eye row was measured off a BARE render (bald default character, no hair to confuse the silhouette): the covered eye spans canvas 355-374, centre 364.5, cross-checked two ways -- mirroring the far eye about the head centre gives 363, and eyeMask.json's stand-south iris rects are 3px in 256-space = 9.75 canvas px, exactly the width of the measured dark runs.  At the shipped -12 the lens centre sat at 350.5, i.e. 14 canvas px (4.3 meta px) LEFT of the eye -- on the temple, tangent to the head silhouette, with the eye buried at the lens's inner edge, which is exactly the 'too far' the owner is describing.  At -8 the lens centre is 363.5 against an eye centre of 364.5: one canvas pixel, 0.3 meta px, dead centre on the eye.  Four meta px is 15% of the lens width -- a nudge, not a relocation.  -8 is the RIGHTMOST value this pass would ship, and the failure going further is not the southwest one: it is not that the lens floats off the face but that the rim crosses the face and reaches the OTHER eye.  v2.3.2417 CORRECTS THE TWO NUMBERS THAT FOLLOWED, and both were wrong in the direction that flatters the choice.  Far-eye clearance at -8 is about 2px, NOT the +4px first written here: that figure compared a lens rim found by DIFFERENCING two renders against an eye found by BRIGHTNESS threshold, and those two edges are not the same edge, so the gap was measured between marks made by different rulers.  2px is still clearance and the failure direction is unchanged -- at -6 the rim clips the far eye's sclera, and by -4 the lens covers it outright -- but the margin at -8 is one rim's width, not four.  And -8 is NOT the only value the pinned assertions admit: -10 passes them too (inFrac 0.024 > 0.02, rightFrac 0.549 < 0.61).  The assertions bound the piece to the face; they do not choose between -10 and -8.  What chooses -8 is the eye-centre measurement above, and -10 is the conservative neighbour if the far eye ever reads tight on a head this pass did not render.  Do not go right of -8.  Proportions hold at 390x664 (overhang -11px vs -14px), so this is not viewport-specific.
